messages.author: 8aa7b9e8ebc839ba
messages.subject: Multistate models in m-array formulation
parts:
Good afternoon,
I have implemented multistate models in State-Space formulation with JAGS following chapter 9 of the book Kéry and Schaub 2012, but the computational cost of the model is 9 days...
I wonder if there is accesible code in the m-array formulation for these models, similar to that of Kéry and Schaub. Thanks in advance,
Blanca

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Multistate models in m-array formulation
parts:
We've had some good success with NIMBLE for multistate models.  NIMBLE supports JAGS/BUGS model syntax but also allows users to provide new functions and distributions from R, which are compiled with the model via C++.  Using this feature, we implemented a Hidden Markov Model distribution, which means one can avoid doing MCMC for the many discrete latent states of multistate models and instead sum their probabilities directly. The approach is described in this paper:  https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10651-016-0353-z, with accompanying code.  In the final example (multistate), with custom efforts NIMBLE was 70-1000 times more efficient than JAGS, depending on specifics such as whether parameters were blocked for more efficient sampling.

-Perry

messages.subject: RE: Multistate models in m-array formulation
parts:
Thank you very much Daniel for your updates. This improvement can make these multistate codes more useful.

 

Best regards,

Jose

De: Daniel Turek [mailto:db...@williams.edu]
Enviado el: miércoles, 22 de noviembre de 2017 16:55
Para: Jose Jimenez Garcia-Herrera; Blanca
CC: Perry de Valpine; Chris Paciorek; hmecology: Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology
Asunto: Re: Multistate models in m-array formulation

Thanks for the issue.  As Perry mentioned, some of the code at https://github.com/danielturek/HMM-MCMC has fallen behind the more recent safeguards that the NIMBLE package now enforces.  I've just pushed some changes to the HMM-MCMC repository, which will get the examples running.  So you should now be able to execute the scripts provided there.

 

Fair warning, however, when running some of the examples (goose and orchid) you'll still see a (frightening looking) error message along the lines of:

"Error in envRefInferField(x, what, getClass(class(x)), selfEnv) : 'getParam_3D_double' is not a valid field or method name for reference class"

 

This message isn't pretty, but it also doesn't prevent the models and MCMCs from running.  It's an error in the "model checking" routine, but everything following should still work fine.  We'll be looking into this issue with the model "checker", and will make appropriate updates to the NIMBLE package to fix it.

 

Thanks for the continued interest in NIMBLE!

 

Daniel
